headline_marked: ME Crisis: [[US and Iran intensify attacks]] as ceasefire deal collapses
headline: ME Crisis: US and Iran intensify attacks as ceasefire deal collapses
summary: US personnel killed in Jordan and civilian targets hit in Kuwait and Saudi Arabia as the risk of all-out war grows.
details: The US and Iran have intensified military strikes after a month-old interim ceasefire deal collapsed last week, raising fears of a return to all-out war in the Middle East.
US Central Command confirmed two personnel were killed and another is missing in Jordan following an Iranian attack. Iran claims to have destroyed US fighter aircraft at the Al Azraq base.
Iran responded by targeting US Gulf allies. In Kuwait, Iranian ballistic missiles and drones hit a US military support center and an oil facility, causing significant damage and injuries to workers.
Saudi Arabia's early warning systems issued alerts for residents in Al-Kharj and Yanbu to seek shelter following an Iranian missile attack, the first on the kingdom in over three months.

The US has carried out seven consecutive days of strikes on Iranian surveillance sites, military logistics, and weapons storage. These strikes have killed three people and wounded eight others in Hormozgan province.
Iran's Health Ministry reports that 50 people have been killed and over 500 injured in US strikes over the past three weeks.
Both nations are now targeting shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical artery for one-fifth of the world's oil supply, leading to a 4% rise in oil prices.
Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, stated that the US would pay for seeking to escalate the conflict, calling President Donald Trump's signature on the previous deal 'utterly worthless'.
caption:
Two US personnel killed and civilian targets hit across the Middle East as the US-Iran ceasefire collapses.

The US and Iran have intensified military strikes after a month-old interim ceasefire deal collapsed last week, raising fears of a return to all-out war in the Middle East.

US Central Command confirmed two personnel were killed and another is missing in Jordan following an Iranian attack. Iran claims to have destroyed US fighter aircraft at the Al Azraq base.

Iran responded by targeting US Gulf allies. In Kuwait, Iranian ballistic missiles and drones hit a US military support center and an oil facility, causing significant damage and injuries to workers.

Saudi Arabia's early warning systems issued alerts for residents in Al-Kharj and Yanbu to seek shelter following an Iranian missile attack, the first on the kingdom in over three months.

The US has carried out seven consecutive days of strikes on Iranian surveillance sites, military logistics, and weapons storage. These strikes have killed three people and wounded eight others in Hormozgan province.

Iran's Health Ministry reports that 50 people have been killed and over 500 injured in US strikes over the past three weeks.

Both nations are now targeting shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical artery for one-fifth of the world's oil supply, leading to a 4% rise in oil prices.

Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, stated that the US would pay for seeking to escalate the conflict, calling President Donald Trump's signature on the previous deal 'utterly worthless'.

headline_marked: 22 goals: [[Mbappe becomes World Cup all-time top scorer]]
headline: 22 goals: Mbappe becomes World Cup all-time top scorer
summary: The French star surpassed Lionel Messi's record to claim the top spot in the tournament's history.
details: Kylian Mbappe has officially become the top scorer in World Cup history. He achieved this milestone on Sunday during the third-place play-off match against England.
The Frenchman netted his second goal of the game to bring his total tally to 22 goals.
This achievement marks a new record, placing him one goal ahead of Argentina's Lionel Messi.
Mbappe has scored these 22 goals across three different World Cup tournaments.
The record-breaking feat comes just before Monday's final, where Lionel Messi is set to play against Spain.
caption:
22 goals and a new world record! Kylian Mbappe is now the greatest goal-scorer in World Cup history.

Kylian Mbappe has officially become the top scorer in World Cup history. He achieved this milestone on Sunday during the third-place play-off match against England.

The Frenchman netted his second goal of the game to bring his total tally to 22 goals.

This achievement marks a new record, placing him one goal ahead of Argentina's Lionel Messi.

Mbappe has scored these 22 goals across three different World Cup tournaments.

The record-breaking feat comes just before Monday's final, where Lionel Messi is set to play against Spain.
